- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >50% negative values) and model forecasts remain flat or upward, adjust downward by 3–5% to account for bearish sentiment pressure.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–4% downward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often lags — apply a 1–2 day lag correction by lowering forecast 1–2 steps ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, if recent 3–5 days show strong downward trend, model often fails to capture momentum — apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5-day average.
- If official events are frequent and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate volatility — reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to reflect event-driven price suppression.
